selection_mode: manual stress test of Concept Engine v3

selected.title: The Forecast in Your Chest
selected.hook: Anxiety often arrives like breaking news: red banner, urgent music, somebody yelling, ‘Something is wrong.’
selected.ruling_metaphor: The body is a landscape of sensors and the mind is a weather station interpreting conditions into a forecast.
selected.mechanism: Constructed-emotion theory models emotional categories as inferences that integrate interoceptive signals, learned concepts, context, memory and prediction.
selected.turn: The feeling is real and worthy of care; the forecast may still be incomplete.
selected.grounding: Feel the chair beneath you, notice your feet, and allow one ordinary breath without requiring it to prove anything.
selected.invitation: When the next strong feeling issues a warning, what is your body forecasting—and what is actually happening outside the window?

why_this_test.summary: This concept simultaneously tests emotional usefulness, emerging-science fidelity, non-directive influence, practical application and motion-rich visual storytelling.
system_capabilities_exercised: science boundary remains visible inside the narration
emotion is validated rather than dismissed
agency is proportionate rather than magical
the viewer receives an observable test rather than a conclusion
visuals carry one coherent weather system with concrete motion
help containers can be generated beyond the video
failure_modes_being_tested: presenting an emerging theory as settled fact
using fear or certainty to produce retention
decorative storm imagery that does not reveal the mechanism

viewer_state.label: Overwhelmed by a predicted future
viewer_state.desired_movement: From treating a feeling as a verdict to examining it as a body-informed prediction.
viewer_state.safe_landing: Feet, chair, breath and one observable fact in the present room.

science_ledger.emerging: Constructed-emotion theory is an influential, evidence-based framework in which bodily signals, context, learning and prediction contribute to emotional categorization.
science_ledger.established_adjacent: Interoception and contextual interpretation contribute to emotional experience, though theories disagree about the architecture and universality of emotion categories.
science_ledger.metaphor: The body as weather landscape and the brain as forecasting station.
science_ledger.evidence_boundary: The framework is debated and does not show that feelings are unreal, deliberately chosen, freely editable or substitutes for medical evaluation.

practical_test.name: Sensation / Prediction / Present Evidence
steps: Name the observable bodily sensation without interpreting it.
Name the event the mind is forecasting.
Name what is verifiably happening in the present room.
Keep all three visible without forcing the feeling to disappear.

example.present_evidence: I am sitting in a room and the conversation has not started.

practical_test.boundary: This is a reflection tool, not diagnosis, treatment or a reason to ignore persistent or concerning symptoms.

visual_grammar.opening_requirement: Bright, immediately legible weather-radar motion with the title unobstructed; no dark text box covering the first image.
moving_subjects: archive cards moving through a sorter
avoid: human footage exceeding half the scenes

success_hypothesis.attention: The newsroom hook retains viewers while scene seven clarifies that the feeling is real.
success_hypothesis.understanding: Viewers distinguish sensation, prediction and evidence without concluding that emotions are fake.
success_hypothesis.reflection: Comments include noticing, testing, curiosity or constructive disagreement rather than agreement alone.
success_hypothesis.application: Viewers report trying the three-part separation in an ordinary situation.
success_hypothesis.autonomy: Dependency, certainty transfer, distress and medical misinterpretation remain low.
success_hypothesis.production: The weather metaphor remains legible across 24 moving, varied scenes with low human dependence.

risk_mitigations: The narration explicitly says the feeling is real and worthy of care.
The narration explicitly rejects the idea that symptoms are chosen or can be smiled away.
The science is labeled emerging and described as one possibility.
The practice asks for observation, not suppression.
The practical tool is explicitly non-clinical.

required_checks: rendered grounding in the final five scenes
all evidence scenes contain source identifiers
